Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached a compact operator-flow diagram (PNG) and a 2-page narrative that covers detection, failover choreography, and control ownership. High level summary below:

- Trigger: node-level telemetry or sidecar KV inconsistency flags automatic soft-fail; if auto-recovery fails, operator initiates controlled failover.
- Control-plane actions (Redwood): cordon node, snapshot KV cache to encrypted objectstore, spin up replacement enclave in same VPC zone, replay minimal KV subset (prefix-only) to maintain low-latency cold-starts.
- Network egress during recovery: egress is strictly limited to Redwood-managed telemetry endpoints (metrics, trace ingestion), and to the customer-configured storage endpoints for KV replay. Tenant traffic to external customer endpoints remains blocked until security gating completes.
- Operator privileges: operators cannot directly access tenant payloads; they operate via limited-control plane APIs audited and subject to HSM-backed key policies. When human intervention is required, session is recorded and an approval ticket is logged.

Attachments included: rfi-enclave-operator-flow-v2.png, egress-evidence-snippets.txt (short URLs and attestations). Marissa, Ben — please confirm the attestation artifact is up-to-date for the diagram (SOC2 reference IDs) and the control-plane evidence we link in the snippets.

Happy to walk through this on a call if useful.

—Jonas
